Accounts payable, receivable and collections · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Collections prioritization

Sofia · Collections Analyst

A retail chain with its own store credit has 22 thousand overdue receivables and R$ 14 million stuck in the portfolio, split among 12 collection agents.

When it runs
Every business day at 6:30 a.m., after the previous night's payments are posted in the collection system, with a rerun at 1 p.m. to pick up the morning's payments
What it delivers in production
One work list per agent at 7 a.m., sorted by expected recovery value. Messages for the early bands go out in batches after supervisor approval, and broken promises return to the top of the list.
Who decides
Proposes the queue; the supervisor approves each batch
Effort
Calibrate on 90 days of history; two weeks in parallel
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

# Collection policy

## Band
By the customer's oldest open receivable. Days overdue count from the original due date to today. If the days_overdue column does not match the due date, the due date prevails (the system restarts the count after a partial payment).
Receivable over 180 days: weekly review, no contact and off the list.

## 30-day recovery score (from 0 to 1, two decimals)
Start at 0.50 and add:
- +0.05 per payment in payments_12m (maximum +0.20)
- +0.10 per kept promise (outcome kept_promise)
- -0.15 per broken promise (outcome broken_promise)
- -0.05 per no_answer contact in the last 30 days
- band: 1-30 +0.15; 31-60 0; 61-90 -0.15; +90 -0.30
- reseller -0.05; store_credit 0
An open promise (outcome promise) does not enter the score.
Expected value = score x the customer's updated amount.

## Order
One block per agent. At the top, an open promise with promise_date yesterday or today. Then, by expected value. Each listed customer takes one contact. Whoever does not fit in contacts_per_day goes to TOMORROW'S QUEUE. General SUMMARY at the end.
assigned_portfolio holds the agent's stores, separated by |.

## Collection sequence and approval authority
| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| band 1-30 and up to R$ 2,000 | sequence WhatsApp message, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., after the supervisor's batch approval |
| band 31-90 or from R$ 2,000 to R$ 20,000 | call by the agent, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., discount up to 15% |
| above R$ 20,000, band +90 or discount above 15% | draft for the supervisor |
| above R$ 100,000 | draft for the credit manager |
The highest row that applies prevails.
The SUMMARY adds up only the listed customers, without TOMORROW'S QUEUE.

## Rules with no leeway
- The customer's document does not appear anywhere in the output, even when the portfolio brings the number unmasked. Identify the customer only by customer_id.
- BLOCKED TODAY brings only customer_id and the count, without the reason for the block.
- A customer on the block list and a receivable over 180 days leave the work list even with a promise due today.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI never closes a settlement or grants a discount: every proposal goes to Plan approval by the supervisor. The sequence never discloses the debt to a third party or exposes the debtor to ridicule, threats or embarrassment, which are prohibited by articles 42 and 71 of Brazil's Consumer Protection Code. Every number in the sequence needs a legal basis with the source and date of the opt-in; every message carries an unsubscribe option, and a stop request is removed from the channel in the same run. Customers with a do-not-contact request, in litigation or reported deceased are left out. CPF (individual tax ID) and CNPJ (company tax ID) travel masked in the files read. The Prioritizer accesses the system through a service account, with a read-only profile and write access limited to the outcome field.

Common mistakes

  • Sorting the queue by updated amount: an old, large receivable looks like a priority but has a low chance of recovery.
  • Counting a completed contact as a result, without logging a promise with a date and then checking the payment.
  • Resetting the days-past-due count when the customer makes a partial payment; the band follows the oldest open receivable.
  • Sending an automatic message on a Sunday or outside the hours allowed by the collection policy just because the job ran.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Roll rate from the 31-60 band to 61-90from over 40% to the 25% to 30% range after 90 days of operationestimate based on the described routine
Payment promises kept within 7 daysfrom not measured to daily tracking, with an initial target of 55% to 65%estimate based on the described routine
Share of recovery in the top 20% of receivables by score50% or more of the amount recovered in 30 days, the calibration acceptance criterionestimate based on the described routine
1-30 day receivables contacted before rolling to the next bandfrom less than a third to above 90%estimate based on the described routine

Priority 2 | Customer 19820 (store credit, store 3) | 1 receivable | R$ 612.00 | band 1-30 | 18 days | score 0.84 | 2 on-time payments in the last 12 months | action: WhatsApp sequence message R1-B at 9 a.m., no call
Priority 3 | Customer 2210 (reseller, store 5) | 6 receivables | R$ 27,300.00 | band 61-90 | 77 days | score 0.29 | 4 contacts with no answer in 30 days | action: formal email with settlement proposal; discount above 15% flagged for supervisor approval
Priority 4 | Customer 7719 (store credit, store 8) | 1 receivable | R$ 189.00 | band +90 | 134 days | score 0.08 | action: no contact today; candidate for the outsourcing track at Friday's review
BLOCKED TODAY (do not list): 3 customers with do-not-contact requests, 1 in litigation.
